Marco Rubio Pushes to Block Low-Cost, High-Speed Broadband

“The FCC is promoting government-owned networks at the possible expense of private sector broadband providers … "

Title is a tad misleading. It's not that Rubio wants to crush low-cost, high-speed broadband, it's that he's concerned about it being in the hands of the government - and potentially a government monopoly. This is a perfectly conservative, perfectly legitimate concern. However, if he really wanted to prove he wasn't in the pocket of big telecom, he could also push against the rules that give them near complete regional monopolies. If the market were allowed to function, I suspect local municipalities wouldn't feel the need to undercut them.

Give me one example of municipal internet that has worsened consumer conditions. Seriously, I can't find a real world example that justifies his actions in any sense.

Right now where I live I have literally only ATT and Comcast to choose from... And shortly after they implement data caps it will be solely ATT for me, which requires a 12 month contract to sign up. Please tell me how municipal internet would make this an issue.

This is 100% a bought and paid for politician and he is selling out his constituents with no shame.

"New hinges rarely squeak", is what I usually hear in response to this. I mean, I'm sure you're right, in that thus far city internet has been an improvement at the consumer level.

It's just that fiscal conservatives, with very good reason, are suspect of government intrusions into what should be a private enterprise. We have a long history of government waste and incompetence we can point back at and say "Mmm-hmm, it sounded like a good idea at the time, but 20 years later how'd that turn out?" Now, if you are of a different political persuasion I'm sure you can understand that if not agree with it, so you can understand how Rubio's position is not necessarily a sign he's a tool for telecoms.

Right now where I live I have literally only ATT and Comcast to choose from... And shortly after they implement data caps it will be solely ATT for me, which requires a 12 month contract to sign up. Please tell me how municipal internet would make this an issue.

This, is entirely my point. The right believes in market competition, and in a healthy marketplace, you should have more than AT&T and Comcast to choose from. More than one potential competitor has been squashed or gobbled up because the rules favor larger corporations. It shouldn't be that way.

You could be right, that Rubio is bought and paid for. I didn't respond to this to shill for Rubio. But you should know, that this one instance doesn't prove what you said. Because it's exactly what I, and most other fiscal conservatives, would say if we were running for president on our own dime with not a person in the world to answer to.

There are some things the private market simply won't do, and providing proper infrastructure is exactly one of them.

Electricity, water, and recently communications were all gimped, only serving areas that were deemed profitable, until eventually government had to get involved. These had far reaching consequences, all of them beneficial to our society as a whole.

Comcast and ATT have 0% reason to innovate or compete (especially since my state explicitly forbids municipal internet) and there is no chance or opportunity for another company to enter the market. God forbid we forget about the massive taxpayer funded boost back in 2007 to get them up to par (in which they simply pocketed).

There is nothing our supposed "free market" can do - we need to turn to municipal internet plain and simple.

You're missing a critical component here: Comcast and AT&T are almost always given monopoly rights to any city, so that others can't compete(Google Fiber has to worm its way around legally to be offered as a completely different category of service than cable or telephone wires in order to get into households). Personally, I'd honestly rather see real, true competition(the power competition where I live makes prices vastly cheaper than the city-owned electricity just a mile or two away), but in a smaller town you're right it's probably going to be easier to hold a municipality-owned company to its end of the bargain if you're going to have any sort of monopoly.
